Validate a Data Frame Against an r4subdata Schema

Source: R/validate_dataset.R
validate_dataset.Rd

Checks that a data frame conforms to the column/type schema of one of the r4subdata reference datasets (as defined by dataset_dictionary()), or to a custom dictionary of the same shape. This is a structural, non-inventive helper: it compares column names and types only and does not check or impose any regulatory values, thresholds, or code lists. It is useful for validating data frames that downstream code builds to look like a shipped dataset (for example a user-constructed evidence table or metadata table) before feeding them to the rest of the R4SUB (Ready for Submission) ecosystem.

Usage

validate_dataset(data, schema, strict = FALSE)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble to validate.

schema

Either the name of an r4subdata dataset (a length-one character, e.g. "evidence_pharma") whose dataset_dictionary() defines the expected schema, or a dictionary tibble/data frame with at least the columns column and type.

strict

Logical. When TRUE, the columns of data must appear in the same order as the schema; an ordering difference is reported as an issue. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A tibble of validation issues with columns issue, column, expected, actual, and message. A zero-row tibble means data conforms to the schema. The returned object also carries a logical "valid" attribute (retrievable with attr(x, "valid")). Possible issue values are "missing_column", "unexpected_column", "type_mismatch", and "column_order".

Details

Type comparison uses the same vocabulary as dataset_dictionary() ("character", "integer", "numeric", "POSIXct"). An integer column satisfies an expected numeric type (integer is a numeric subtype), but a double column does not satisfy an expected integer type.

See also

dataset_dictionary(), list_datasets()

Examples

# A shipped dataset validates cleanly against its own schema.
validate_dataset(adam_metadata, "adam_metadata")
#> # A tibble: 0 × 5
#> # ℹ 5 variables: issue <chr>, column <chr>, expected <chr>, actual <chr>,
#> #   message <chr>

# A data frame with a missing column and a wrong type reports issues.
bad <- data.frame(
  dataset = "ADSL", variable = "AGE",
  label = "Age", type = "Num", length = "8"
)
validate_dataset(bad, "adam_metadata")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   issue          column expected  actual    message                             
#>   <chr>          <chr>  <chr>     <chr>     <chr>                               
#> 1 missing_column format character NA        Column 'format' is required by the …
#> 2 type_mismatch  length integer   character Column 'length' should be integer b…
